QuestionStmt.S: In a triangle $ABC$, with usual notations, $3b = a + c$, then $\cot\frac{A}{2} \cdot \cot\frac{C}{2} =$

Solution.S:
$$\cot \left( \frac{A}{2} \right) \cdot \cot \left( \frac{C}{2} \right)$$

$$= \frac{1}{\tan \left( \frac{A}{2} \right) \cdot \tan \left( \frac{C}{2} \right)}$$

$$= \sqrt{\frac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}} \times \frac{s(s-c)}{(s-a)(s-b)} \quad \text{... [By half angle formulae]}$$

$$= \sqrt{\frac{s^2}{(s-b)^2}}$$

$$\therefore \cot \left( \frac{A}{2} \right) \cdot \cot \left( \frac{C}{2} \right) = \frac{s}{s-b} \quad \cdots (i)$$

$$2s = a + b + c$$

$$\Rightarrow 2s = 3b + b \quad \cdots [a + c = 3b \text{ (given)}]$$

$$\Rightarrow 2s = 4b$$

$$\Rightarrow s = 2b$$

Substituting $s = 2b$ in equation (i), we get

$$\cot \left( \frac{A}{2} \right) \cdot \cot \left( \frac{C}{2} \right) = \frac{2b}{2b-b} = \frac{2b}{b} = 2$$
